# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->

Argentina's national population censuses are the main source of demographic and social information with national and provincial coverage over several decades, but their historical results are scattered across printed books, scanned PDFs, spreadsheets, and closed systems, with structures and classifications that change from one census round to the next. Researchers, teachers, public agencies, and journalists who want to work with these data must locate the original sources, transcribe and reshape tables by hand, and validate the results before any analysis can begin. ARcenso, an R package developed through the rOpenSci Champions Program, started to close this gap by providing reproducible access to the official tables published by INDEC, but it currently covers only the 1970 census, at the national and provincial levels, and the 1980 census at the national level.

This project will complete ARcenso's coverage of Argentina's 20th-century censuses and prepare the package for its first release on CRAN and R-universe. The work is organized around three complementary lines. First, we will incorporate the 1960 census, recently made available by INDEC, the 1980 census at the provincial level, and the complete 1991 census, so that the package will offer every census from 1960 to 1991 at the national and provincial levels. Second, we will redesign how census tables are stored: numeric values will be stored as numbers rather than text, and tables will be consolidated and compressed, which keeps the package within CRAN's size limits as coverage grows while also making the data easier to use. Third, we will replace the current manual conversion of tables with a semi-automated workflow in which AI tools propose the extraction and tidy structure of each table, while the versioned output is a deterministic R script, validated against the totals published by INDEC and reviewed by a team member. AI is part of the development process, not of the package, so end users do not depend on it, and reproducibility and quality are preserved.

The minimum viable product, due by April 2027, is a release on R-universe with the new data format and the 1991 national-level tables processed through the pipeline, keeping the current user interface unchanged. Full census coverage is due by August 2027, and submission to CRAN by September 2027. Deliverables also include updated documentation and vignettes, a documented conversion pipeline in the repository, and blog posts on the R Consortium blog.

The project will run from January to September 2027 and requires 245 hours of work, split equally between the two team members, for a total of USD 5,500, paid against three deliverable-based milestones. Beyond the immediate results, the pipeline developed here will allow the remaining stages of the package roadmap, covering the 2001, 2010, and 2022 censuses, to be completed consistently and at lower cost.
